hints.text: Adding means putting two amounts together to find the total.
Start at $3$ and count up $4$ more: $4, 5, 6, 7$.
After counting up four steps from $3$, you land on the number that comes just after $6$.

solution.title: Identify the operation
solution.detail: The plus sign tells us to add the two numbers together.

questions.prompt: Liam has 2 red apples and 5 green apples. How many apples does Liam have in all?

hints.text: When the question asks how many in all, you bring the groups together.
Combine the red and green apples: $2 + 5$.
$2$ apples plus $5$ more apples lands on the number right before $8$.

solution.title: Find the totals
solution.detail: Liam has $2$ red apples and $5$ green apples.

questions.prompt: What number, when added to four, gives nine?

hints.text: We need a missing part. Think: what added to four makes nine?
If you start at four, how many more do you count to reach nine?
Counting up from four — five, six, seven, eight, nine — is five steps.

solution.title: Read the question
solution.detail: We need a number that adds to four to make nine.

solution.title: Count up
solution.detail: From four, count: five, six, seven, eight, nine — that is five steps.

questions.prompt: Maya has 6 crayons. Her friend gives her 2 more. How many crayons does Maya have now?

hints.text: Getting more means the total goes up — that is addition.
Add the crayons she had to the new ones: $6 + 2$.
Two more than $6$ is the number right after $7$.

solution.title: Identify the operation
solution.detail: Receiving more crayons means we add.

hints.text: Adding $1$ to a number means counting one more.
What is the next number after $8$?
Right after $8$ is the answer — it is just below $10$.

solution.title: Add one
solution.detail: Adding $1$ moves to the next number.

questions.prompt: Theo runs 4 laps in the morning and 3 laps in the afternoon. How many laps did Theo run that day?

hints.text: Running more laps means the total grows. Which operation does that?
Add the morning laps to the afternoon laps: $4 + 3$.
Three more than $4$ is the number just before $8$.

solution.title: Combine the two parts of the day
solution.detail: Morning laps and afternoon laps are added together.

questions.prompt: Which number sentence makes a sum of $6$?

hints.text: Find each total, then look for the one that equals $6$.
Try each: $3 + 2 = 5$, $5 + 2 = 7$. Keep going.
$4 + 2$ makes $6$ because two more than $4$ is $6$.
Adding zero is special — it does not change anything.
Zero means none, so the total stays the same as the other number.
If you start with $5$ and add nothing, you still have $5$.

solution.title: Zero rule
solution.detail: Adding zero leaves a number unchanged.

questions.prompt: Noor saw 3 ducks at the pond. Then 6 more ducks waddled over. How many ducks were at the pond then?

hints.text: More ducks arriving means the group gets bigger — add.
Add the first ducks to the new arrivals: $3 + 6$.
Six more than $3$ is one less than $10$.

solution.title: Group the ducks
solution.detail: Original ducks plus the new ones.

hints.text: Two parts come together — add them.
Start at $7$ and count up $2$ more: $8, 9$.
Two more than $7$ is the number just before $10$.

solution.title: Count up
solution.detail: $7$, then $8, 9$. Two steps takes you to $9$.
